chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Habib narrated to us. He said: Tamim ibn Bahlul narrated to us. He said: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih ibn Abi Salama al-Nusaybi narrated to us. He said: Abu 'Awana narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from 'A'isha. He said:

I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him and his family) say: I am the master of the former and the latter peoples, and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib is the master of the deputies. He is my brother, my inheritor, and my vicegerent (khalifa) over my nation. His wilaya is obligatory, following him is a virtue, and loving him is a means of approach to God. His party is the Party of God, his Shi'a are the supporters of God, his friends are the friends of God, and his enemies are the enemies of God. He is the Imam of the Muslims, the master of the believers, and their commander after me.

key_terms.حِزْبُ اللَّهِ: Hizb Allah (Party of God) — a term from Q. 5:56 applied here to 'Ali's followers
key_terms.خَلِيفَتِي: My khalifa — vicegerent, a term indicating succession to prophetic authority
key_terms.سَيِّدُ الْوَصِيِّينَ: Master of the Deputies/Successors — the highest successor among all divine emissaries' successors
key_terms.وَسِيلَةٌ: Wasila — a means of spiritual approach or intercession to God
key_terms.وَلَايَتُهُ فَرِيضَةٌ: His wilaya is obligatory — a core Shi'a creedal assertion that accepting 'Ali's authority is a religious duty

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about 'Ali ibn Abi Talib's authority and status according to al-Amali of al-Saduq?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through a lengthy chain ending with 'A'isha, records the Prophet Muhammad's declaration of his own supreme status and the divinely ordained authority of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. The Prophet proclaims 'Ali as the Master of Deputies (wasis), his brother, heir, and khalifa over the entire Muslim community, and declares his wilaya (guardianship) as a religious obligation. This hadith establishes three tiers of obligation regarding 'Ali: wilaya as mandatory, following him as meritorious, and loving him as a spiritual means (wasila) of drawing closer to God.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Yahya b. Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Bakr b. `Abdullah b. Habib narrated to us. He said: Tamim b. Bahlul narrated to us. He said: `Abdullah b. Salih b. Abi Salama al-Nusaybi narrated to us. He said: Abu `Awana from Abi Bishr narrated to us from Sa`id b. Jubayr from `A’isha.

She said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (s) say: I am the master of the former and the latter peoples. `Ali b. Abi Talib is the Master of Deputies. He is my brother, my inheritor, and my vicegerent (khalifa) over my Nation. His wilaya is obligatory. Following him is a virtue. Loving him is a way to Allah. His party is the Party of Allah, his Shi`a are the supporters of Allah, his friends are the friends of Allah, and his enemies are the enemies of Allah. He is the Imam of the Muslims, the Master of the Believers and their emir after me.
